title: Synergistic effect and comparative study of CoMn2O4 and MnCo2O4 spinel nanoparticles as promising materials for electrochemical hydrogen storage
desc: The development of stable electrode materials with high performance, based on transition metals, is vital for advancing energy storage applications. This study reports the synthesis of CoMn2O4 and MnCo2O4 spinel nanoparticles (SNPs) via a wet-chemistry method, and investigates their performance as electrode materials for electrochemical hydrogen storage. XRD analysis confirmed the formation of highly crystalline spinel structures for both samples, with an average crystallite size of 32 nm. FE-SEM imaging revealed that the CoMn2O4 and MnCo2O4 SNPs exhibit an agglomerated, polyhedral morphology, with mean particle sizes of 49 and 53 nm, respectively. BET analysis confirmed the mesoporous structure of the samples. Electrochemical studies, including cyclic voltammetry and chronopotentiometry, demonstrated excellent electrochemical performance. CoMn2O4 and MnCo2O4 SNPs exhibited a specific capacitance (Csp) of 417 and 424 F/g, at a scan rate of 10 mV/s. Furthermore, CoMn2O4 and MnCo2O4 SNPs showcased hydrogen storage capacities of 1930 and 1594 mAh/g, respectively, following 10 charge–discharge cycles. These results highlight the potential of the samples as promising candidates for electrochemical hydrogen storage.
